back: A device whose resistance or p.d. changes with a physical quantity so that it can be measured or detected electrically.
LDR: resistance falls as light intensity rises. NTC thermistor: resistance falls (non-linearly) as temperature rises.
Stretched: longer and thinner, so $R = \rho L/A$ rises. At constant volume $\Delta R/R \approx 2\varepsilon$.
A p.d. appears across a crystal (e.g. quartz) when it is compressed or stretched; it changes shape when a p.d. is applied.
$V_{\text{out}} = V_{\text{in}}\dfrac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}$ (output across $R_2$, negligible current drawn)
Recording a system's output against known values of the quantity, then reading unknowns from the calibration curve.
A small current in the coil closes contacts in a separate high-current circuit; a reverse diode across the coil protects against the induced e.m.f. at switch-off.
Sensor → processing (divider, comparator or amplifier) → output (relay, LED, meter).
